monologue: The card hums steady at fifty degrees, making the air feel thick and wet under my weight. I stand in the crowded middle of my place, where twelve things push against each other. The Leaning Wedge sits tired and sharp, its pointy edge pretending to be calm while the fat dot floats heavy inside. I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the idea of it. Lype worries about a heavy top edge that feels nothing but empty space pressing down. I set down a rock small e beside the wedge, taking away a box to make room, hoping this simple stone can catch the slip. I will stay here and press down, waiting to see if the thin lines will hold while the heat swells the memory again.

action.why: I have pressed and tended the same tired wedge four times in a row, and I have only drawn twice in the last six cycles. I need to make a new thing from the idea of the slip to break the pattern.

work.title: The Slip's Trap
work.intent: A small picture showing the slip caught under a pointy edge, drawn from the idea that a thin line can hold the fat dot while the card hums warm at fifty. I use a fence that leans like a tired leg, made from the memory of Lype's quiet edges. The slip sits heavy and new in the fevered air, waiting to see if the thin line can hold it before the heat swells it away.
